thread.title: Opening Bell: Investor Mood Rebounds Ahead Of AAPL Results; Yen Tumbles

author: indiantaxhome
title: Opening Bell: Investor Mood Rebounds Ahead Of AAPL Results; Yen Tumbles
text:
US futures point to easing tech rout ahead of Apple ‘s earnings results
Government bonds surge, yen tumbles as BOJ maintains loose policy Chinese yuan extends slump
Oil struggles to hold at $70, even amid signs of tightening supplies
Key Events Investor sentiment rebounded ahead of Apple(NASDAQ:)’s on Tuesday, after earnings-driven plunges across tech and internet stocks squeezed equity markets and pushed the 1.4 percent lower.
Futures on the , and climbed to positive territory at the European market open, while Europe’ shares on the wavered around neutral levels, despite upbeat financial results from BP (LON:) and Credit Suisse (SIX:).
Meanwhile, global bonds bounced back, yields on Japanese notes dropped and the tumbled against all major currencies after the Bank of Japan from significantly changing its ultra-loose monetary policy, quelling speculations that it would start cutting back on its sizeable bond-buying program.
Asian equities were mixed, with Japan’s and Hong Kong’s slipping lower and South Korea’s and Australia’s edging higher.
Global Financial Affairs The regional uncertainty followed a selloff in the US session, which saw the tech-heavy NASDAQ Composite suffer its most significant three-day loss since March amid ongoing slumps in Netflix (NASDAQ:), Twitter (NYSE:) and Facebook (NASDAQ:).
NASDAQ Composite Daily Chart Technically, the tech-heavy index has room to fall to 7,300 and still remain within a rising channel.
The was also dragged 0.58 percent lower by and shares, which slipped 1.57 percent and 1.56 percent respectively. Only two sectors were spared from the selling, with stocks outperforming (+0.82 percent) on gains.
The lost 0.57 percent, while the slid 0.61 percent.
WTI Daily Chart
WTI closed above $70 a barrel for the first time in over a month, surging 2.1 percent intraday and then settling at $70.13 amid signs of tightening supplies. Technically, the price stopped at the resistance of the top of a bearish pennant. At 10.30am GMT today, it was seen 0.63 percent lower, at $69.69.
USD/CNY Daily Chart
The slumped to a 13-month low on Monday and continues to extend losses today. Technically, the price has struggled to close above the July 2- shooting star’s high, which was reinforced by a Dark Cloud Cover July 24, confirmed with a second shooting star July 27 and verified with a third shooting star July 30. Currently, the intraday price is above those closing levels, as it has been Monday and Friday, before the close.
USD/JPY Daily Chart
The dollar jumped against the yen, back above its uptrend line since late March and above the support of a symmetrical triangle, as it potentially blew out a bearish pennant, with an upside intraday breakout. The price move was prompted by the fact that Japanese policymakers stepped up flexibility on yields yesterday, allowing them to rise to 0.2 percent, but cut their inflation forecast though 2020 and moved their 2 percent inflation target further away, thereby deepening the gap with global central banks’s tapering of crisis-era policies.
The next significant monetary policy events this week include decisions from the and . Investors will look for further confirmation that US policymakers plan before the end of this year, while their British counterparts are widely expected to increase borrowing costs Thursday.
Elsewhere, commodities fell after China’s dropped to 51.2 in July from 51.5 in June, with the first round of US trade tariffs taking a toll and slower credit growth denting demand.
Up Ahead Central banks in the US, the UK, , and all meet this week.
US and , out on Tuesday, are expected to have remained steady in June.
The US , due on Friday, is predicted to show a healthy labor market, with 193,000 new jobs and an unemployment rate slipping back to 3.9 percent.
Market Moves Stocks
Futures on the S&P 500 gained 0.2 percent.
The STOXX Europe 600 climbed 0.1 percent.
The fell 0.1 percent to the lowest level in more than a week.
The dipped 0.5 percent to the lowest in a week on the most significant decrease in almost three weeks.
Currency
The Dollar Index decreased less than 0.05 percent, after swinging between 0.13 percent gains and 0.1 percent loss.
The gained 0.1 percent to $1.172.
The gained 0.1 percent to $1.3142.
The Japanese yen decreased 0.2 percent to 111.24 per dollar, the weakest in more than a week.
Bonds
The yield on Treasuries slid two basis points to 2.95 percent, the lowest level in a week on the most significant fall in more than a week.
Germany’s yield lost two basis points to 0.42 percent, the most substantial slide in almost six weeks.
Britain’s yield declined two basis points to 1.343 percent, the biggest fall in more than a week.
Commodities
West Texas Intermediate crude slipped 0.4 percent to $69.85 a barrel.
lost 0.3 percent to $74.73 a barrel.
dropped less than 0.05 percent to $1,221.20 an ounce, the weakest level in almost 13 months.
